region: Burdett · Seneca Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Damiani Wine Cellars sits on the east side of Seneca Lake, on the warm stretch of shoreline locals call the Banana Belt. It is the work of two neighbours who grew up on the land they now farm: winemaker Lou Damiani, who planted his first vinifera vines in 1996, and grower Phil Davis, whose father grew grapes for Taylor and Great Western decades ago and who planted the following year. From the start the winery made its name with red wines, a bold choice in a region best known for Riesling.

The 2023 Cabernet Franc draws on vineyards on both the east and west sides of Seneca Lake. The grapes were fermented in one-ton bins with native yeast, with about 10% whole clusters and a 20% saignée, bleeding off some juice to concentrate the rest. The wine then spent 12 months in neutral French oak, so the fruit is not masked by new wood, and was bottled unfined and unfiltered at 12.5% alcohol.

The winery’s note describes rustic aromas of stewed berries and wood spice with cocoa and cigar box, then savoury, meaty dark fruit with bramble, sweet spice and clove, carried by bright acidity and generous tannins. Cabernet Franc has become one of the Finger Lakes’ calling cards, and in 2026 James Suckling’s New York Cabernet Franc report named Damiani among the region’s top producers of the grape.
